tasks.commitBody:
The three location inputs now suggest previously used venues via
native <datalist> — the open-ended case standing rule 1 does not
govern (no canonical venue vocabulary can exist), built with rule
2's native answer; the deleted <Autocomplete> stays deleted.

On the agenda page both create forms share one suggestion set
derived from the already-loaded agenda items (deduplicated, blanks
dropped, no new fetch). The event-detail route has no location
corpus in memory (confirmed by PO and research independently), so
per the PO ruling it takes a lazy fetch: collective-scoped location
values requested on FIRST FOCUS of the field only — never on page
load — bounded at realistic scale (~150-450 short strings per
collective over 2-3 years, per data-manager census), degrading
silently to a plain input on failure.

The criterion that outranks the rest, pinned by test: a brand-new
venue types and saves exactly as before — byte-identical, no
warning, no friction. Suggestions are convenience over an
inherently open field, never a step toward a closed list.

Live gate (Joosep): start typing 'Hop…' in any of the three
location fields — Hopneri Maja offers itself; a never-used venue
still types straight through.
